headline: 255 votes: Mirza Fakhrul elected Bangladesh's 23rd president
summary: The veteran politician wins a contested parliamentary vote, the first of its kind in 35 years, to step into Bangabhaban.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh, securing 255 votes in a parliamentary election.
This marks the first time in 35 years that a president has been elected through a contested vote among Members of Parliament.
Former interim government advisor Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus has extended his heartfelt congratulations to the President-elect.
Dr. Yunus praised Fakhrul's five decades of political experience, organizational skills, and leadership during times of crisis.
He noted that Fakhrul's background as an academic and experienced politician would uphold the dignity of the state's highest constitutional office.
The President-elect has also received congratulations from the United Kingdom and China, as well as the Jamaat-e-Islami ameer.
Following the announcement of the results, the Prime Minister and opposition leaders were seen embracing in a show of unity.
caption:
A historic win for Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, who secures 255 votes to become the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh, securing 255 votes in a parliamentary election.

This marks the first time in 35 years that a president has been elected through a contested vote among Members of Parliament.

Former interim government advisor Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus has extended his heartfelt congratulations to the President-elect.

Dr. Yunus praised Fakhrul's five decades of political experience, organizational skills, and leadership during times of crisis.

He noted that Fakhrul's background as an academic and experienced politician would uphold the dignity of the state's highest constitutional office.

The President-elect has also received congratulations from the United Kingdom and China, as well as the Jamaat-e-Islami ameer.

Following the announcement of the results, the Prime Minister and opposition leaders were seen embracing in a show of unity.

headline: BNP appoints Ruhul Kabir Rizvi as acting secretary general
summary: The appointment comes after Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stepped down from the post to contest the presidential election.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has appointed Ruhul Kabir Rizvi as its acting secretary general, effective immediately.
In a notice issued on Thursday, the party announced that Rizvi, a member of the National Standing Committee, was nominated for the role according to the party's constitution.
The position had been vacant since August 13, when former secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stepped down to formally announce his candidacy for the presidential election.
Rizvi's appointment follows a period of speculation within the party as he was already serving as the senior joint secretary general.
Additionally, the party's highest policy-making body, the National Standing Committee, recently included four new leaders: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Aman Ullah Aman, Farhad Halim, and Md. Ismail Jabiullah.
caption:
Ruhul Kabir Rizvi takes over as the acting secretary general of the BNP.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has appointed Ruhul Kabir Rizvi as its acting secretary general, effective immediately.

In a notice issued on Thursday, the party announced that Rizvi, a member of the National Standing Committee, was nominated for the role according to the party's constitution.

The position had been vacant since August 13, when former secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stepped down to formally announce his candidacy for the presidential election.

Rizvi's appointment follows a period of speculation within the party as he was already serving as the senior joint secretary general.

Additionally, the party's highest policy-making body, the National Standing Committee, recently included four new leaders: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Aman Ullah Aman, Farhad Halim, and Md. Ismail Jabiullah.
